land.text: Lotharingia, which Arnulf cut out of East Francia for his son Zwentibold at the Diet of Worms in May 895

predecessors.note: East Francia held Lotharingia from the deposition of Charles the Fat in 887 (Lotharingia page); the east-franks dossier records a split and a vassal_start in May 895. The kingdom takes up the Lotharingian name of Lothair II's realm (855-869, dossier kingdom-of-lotharingia, still to be written) but no page links the two as one state.

successors.note: 900: 'After Zwentibold's death, King Louis the Child ruled over Lotharingia' and, from 903, the kingdom was administered by Count Gebhard, who received the title of Duke of Lorraine (Zwentibold page). The Lotharingia page: 'The kingdom then ceased to exist and became a duchy.'

capitals.name: Aachen
capitals.note: UNVERIFIED for Zwentibold: neither the Lotharingia page nor the Zwentibold page names his seat. The only Lotharingian seat on the Lotharingia page is Aachen, for Lothair II ('Lothair II ruled from Aachen'); the dot is a placeholder for the kingdom's old royal city.

rulers.name: Zwentibold
rulers.title: king of Lotharingia (Arnulf's illegitimate son)
rulers.note: Crowned by Arnulf at the Diet of Worms, May 895 (Arnulf page); the Zwentibold page also has him receiving the Lotharingian royal title in 893, so the dates conflict. Slain by Count Reginar I of Hainault and Odoacer on the Meuse near Susteren; 13 August 900 (Lotharingia page; the Zwentibold page gives the date only in its infobox).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 895-898: Cliopatria draws Zwentibold's Lotharingia as a Middle Franks shape for 899 only and gives the same land to the East Franks in 892-898. The Arnulf page: at the Diet of Worms in May 895 Arnulf 'crowned his illegitimate son Zwentibold as the king of Lotharingia'; the Lotharingia page: he 'ruled semi-independently until he was overthrown and killed'. The 899 outline holds from May 895; the east-franks dossier subtracts it from its own keyframes (new east-franks_895) and keeps it as East Frankish vassal land (lighter tint). Moved here from the middle-franks dossier after the review (eu-07-d).

correction.text: Lotharingia as Zwentibold's sub-kingdom from May 895

keyframe_review.note: 124,041 km2 (538 cells at H3 resolution 5: France 157, Netherlands 146, Belgium 109, Germany 109, Luxembourg 12), 899 only. The Lotharingia page describes the region (before the final division) as 'present-day Lorraine (France), Luxembourg, parts of Switzerland' and further lands; the shape has no Swiss cells, and no page gives an area or a boundary for Zwentibold's kingdom. Right as drawn for 899 and, by the previous keyframe, from May 895; the shape passes to east-franks in the drawing from 900 (the year of an event is the first year of the new shape), although Zwentibold fell only on 13 August 900. The middle-franks dossier reviews this same Cliopatria shape as wrong for Middle Francia, because it is this state's.

ledger.note: 895, May: Arnulf crowns his son Zwentibold king of Lotharingia. At the Diet of Worms in May 895 'he crowned his illegitimate son Zwentibold as the king of Lotharingia' (Arnulf page); the Lotharingia page: 'In 895, he appointed his illegitimate son Zwentibold as the king of Lotharingia'. The Zwentibold page also has him receive the royal title in 893 and says 'the rule of King Zwentibold was enforced by his father', against local nobles, with the archbishops of Cologne and Trier on his side. The land is the 538 cells of Cliopatria's Middle Franks shape of 899; east-franks records the matching split.

900, 13 August: Lotharingia passes to Louis the Child. Count Reginar I of Hainault and Odoacer 'rose against Zwentibold and slew him in battle' on the Meuse near Susteren; 'After Zwentibold's death, King Louis the Child ruled over Lotharingia' (Zwentibold page); the Louis the Child page: 'Louis succeeded Zwentibold in 900'. East-franks records the matching gain (August 900).

900, 13 August: the kingdom of Zwentibold ends. He 'ruled semi-independently until he was overthrown and killed by Reginar on August 13, 900. The kingdom then ceased to exist and became a duchy' (Lotharingia page); Gebhard governs it from 903 (Zwentibold page).

wars.name: Overthrow of Zwentibold
belligerents: Reginar I of Hainault and Odoacer
wars.outcome: Count Reginar I of Hainault and Odoacer slew Zwentibold in battle on the Meuse near Susteren (13 August 900); Lotharingia passed to Louis the Child and became a duchy (Gebhard, 903).
wars.note: The pages give no campaign and move no border beyond the change of ruler; the entry records that it was considered. Moved here from the middle-franks dossier after the review (eu-07-d).

certainty.note: Zwentibold's kingdom is drawn as Cliopatria's outline of 899; no page gives a boundary for it.

sources.title: Arnulf of Carinthia
sources.note: Diet of Worms, May 895: Arnulf crowns Zwentibold king of Lotharingia; infobox 'King of Lotharingia 887-894'.

sources.title: Lotharingia
sources.note: Zwentibold appointed in 895, 'ruled semi-independently' until killed by Reginar on 13 August 900; 'The kingdom then ceased to exist and became a duchy'; no capital or boundary for 895-900.

sources.title: Zwentibold
sources.note: Follow-up after review: kingdom granted in 895 (royal title 893 on the same page), rule enforced by his father, slain by Reginar I and Odoacer on the Meuse near Susteren, Louis the Child ruled Lotharingia afterwards, Gebhard from 903; no seat named.

notes: Kingdom of Lotharingia under Zwentibold (eu-07-d), split off after the review from the middle-franks dossier, which had joined Lothair I's Middle Francia (843-855) and Zwentibold's Lotharingia (895-900) in one 843-900 life with a 39-year hole. Cliopatria's Middle Franks row has two shapes: 850-859 (Middle Francia, right only to 855) and 899 (this state). Both dossiers list the Cliopatria Name; the validator therefore warns that middle-franks_850 has no verdict here (it belongs to middle-franks), and middle-franks reviews middle-franks_899 as wrong for Middle Francia. Pages: Arnulf of Carinthia, Lotharingia, Zwentibold, Louis the Child (four of the batch's pages, reopened for the split). Design decided with east-franks: Zwentibold's kingdom is a separate state and East Frankish vassal land (lighter tint) from May 895 to 13 August 900. The east-franks keyframes subtract Middle Franks 899 from 895 to 899 (so the 538 cells are drawn once, by this dossier), and east-franks has a split and a vassal_start in May 895 and a vassal_end and gain in August 900. Year convention: the year of an event is the first year of the new shape, so the keyframes here run 895-899 and east-franks_900 holds Lotharingia again from 900. The alternative (not taken): leave Lotharingia as direct East Frankish land, drop this dossier, the vassal_start/vassal_end pair and the middle-franks 895-900 phase. If the orchestrator prefers one Lotharingian state, this dossier can be merged into kingdom-of-lotharingia (Lothair II, 855-869, still unwritten): the Lotharingia page covers Lothair II's kingdom, Zwentibold's kingdom and the duchy in one article, but the Treaties of Meerssen (870) and Ribemont (880) put the north in East and West Frankish hands between them. Not settled. No page names Zwentibold's seat (Aachen is a flagged placeholder) or his boundary; the Zwentibold page dates his kingship to 895 in one sentence and gives him the royal title in 893 in another; the date of death, 13 August 900, is in the Lotharingia page's text and in the Zwentibold infobox. The wikidata id is the Cliopatria row's (Q6673921), which Cliopatria ties to the Lotharingia article. Family france is the middle-franks dossier's, for continuity with the Cliopatria row. Gazetteer: all names used resolve (Cliopatria shapes only).
